items.title: Activation contract for extension-contributed Space sidebar elements
items.summary: Specification 4763-4866 requires a Plugin's sidebar element to open an arbitrary configured page/URL, an authorised app surface, an authored CUI page or a generative page, or invoke an Automation. The stable identity model already exists (Haven.Core ExtensionSidebarContribution: SidebarItemId/Label/IconKey/TargetKind/TargetId, carried on ExtensionPackageManifest.SidebarContributions) and per-Space visibility exists as SpaceCapabilityBinding(CapabilityId = Manifest.PackageId, Kind = Plugin, Override). What is missing is the runtime contract: an IBrowseNativeAppContentSession such as the Spaces session has no host hook to navigate its own tab to an arbitrary address or to open another app surface, and no reviewed service resolves ExtensionSidebarTargetKind to an authorised target. The Home launcher opens apps through a different, Browse-host-owned path, so reusing it from Spaces would be an invented channel. Implementation has therefore landed only the authored area and stable identity projection (commit aec18695, renders nothing until a projection is supplied); no disabled placeholder rows and no fake activation were shipped. Owner decision needed: which typed host contract owns sidebar-element activation (a session-level open-address/open-app-surface callback, a shared navigation service, or an extension runtime resolver), and which target kinds are in scope for the Spaces sidebar now versus the Plugins milestones (F08/H06). Affected change held: wiring spaces.sidebarItems from the attached-extension projection in Haven.Desktop and implementing spaces.open-sidebar-item in the Spaces session.
items.resolution: Owner direction 2026-10-19: DEC-014 described an implementation gap in already-required behaviour, and routine engineering decisions are authorised under existing policy. Resolved by reusing the existing typed host navigation contract rather than creating a competing framework: BrowseNavigationIntent plus BrowseNativeWorkspace.QueueNavigation, the same path the Home launcher already uses, passed into SpacesBrowseAppContentFactory and the Spaces session as a narrow optional extension. Commits 9fc92762 and 06e7bac8. Remaining scope on the requirement, tracked as implementation work rather than a product decision: Automation and GenerativePage target kinds are not yet opened, and no native journey has been driven with a real attached extension.

Keep the consent step, but make each app's default destination the Home-workspace app folder that already exists (~/9to1/Boards), named by board title, with the private draft retained as recovery - no new consent prompt, and the created folders finally used.

items.summary: Owner model, clarified 29 October: no Files 'connect' step at all. On install the app creates a 9to1 folder under Documents automatically; everything saves there unless the user picks another location; and if the user MOVES that 9to1 folder, the app must find where it went and register it there instead of Documents.
items.verbatim_owner_request: I meant you shouldn't have to go into files and click "connect" - it should automatically create a "9to1" folder under documents when the user installs the deb. And then everything is saved to that unless the user picks another location. And if the user moves that 9to1 folder the app finds where it's saved and registers it there instead of documents. || FINAL REFINEMENT: if the user already has a 9to1 directory in documents, it shouldn't delete that and attempt to override it. inspect what's already there and add any missing directories. if it's already populated with a bunch of user-chosen directories that aren't app names, it should create a separate apps folder and put the app directories in there. if the 9to1 folder goes missing, it should show a screen when the user selects files saying "9to1 directory missing - Re-locate or create new" and give the user the option to either point to the new location (if not detected automatically) or create a new one. This should only show for existing copies where the 9to1 folder was detected but then later disappeared. For new installs, this folder is created/detected automatically without the need for user input.
items.measured_fact: Boards artefacts do exist, but only in a private hash-named subtree: ~/.local/share/9to1-development/profile/Boards/profiles/5018c35df725e59bd1f77c32a5ec0f6198116365e004c38910681edbf455395c/drafts/*.9to1board (4 drafts plus 3 conflict copies). There is no Files-visible Boards folder in the Home Files store at all. So a surface that says 'saved locally' with no path, over a directory named by a 64-character hash, is exactly the reported complaint: the files are saved, the user cannot see where, and the folder they look in is empty.
items.tension: The 27 October headline correction says Boards must create and save WITHOUT connecting Files, an account or a dedicated Boards folder. This later explicit owner direction asks for a Files folder step at creation. Both are owner authority; the later one amends the former for the create path, and the resolution below preserves both intents.
planned_resolution_not_yet_implemented: default save root: a 9to1 folder under the user's Documents, created automatically with per-app subfolders, with no Files connect, no account and no setup gate

created by the app at first run rather than by the package: the shipped .deb deliberately has no maintainer scripts and a package must not write into a user's home, so the first launch of the installed build performs the creation. The behaviour the owner asked for is the same; the mechanism is recorded honestly

Documents may be absent or non-standard: resolve it through the XDG user directories when present, otherwise create it, and if the home itself is not writable fall back to the private app data root and say so on the surface rather than failing silently
user override: choosing another location is stored as the registered root and is always displayed; a board that has never been placed shows its actual draft path, never a bare 'saved locally'

relocation discovery: the 9to1 root carries a marker file holding a stable root id; if the registered path disappears, the app scans plausible parents (Documents, home, Desktop, the last known parent and any directory that already contains a registered 9to1 child) for the marker, and when it matches it re-registers the new path instead of recreating one under Documents; more than one match must be presented, never guessed
migration: the existing drafts (profile/Boards/profiles/<64-hex>/drafts/*.9to1board plus conflict copies) stay openable and are re-pointed into the new root; nothing is deleted or silently moved
never destructive on an existing 9to1 folder: it is inspected and only missing subfolders are added; no delete, no replace, no takeover of an existing directory or its contents

foreign content is respected: if the existing 9to1 folder already holds the user's own directories rather than app directories, the app does not mix its app folders in beside them - it creates a separate apps folder and puts the app directories inside that

recovery screen only for a previously-detected root that later disappeared, raised when the user opens Files: '9to1 directory missing - Re-locate or create new', offering either to point at the new location when automatic detection did not find it, or to create a new one
a fresh install never shows that screen and needs no user input: the folder is created or detected silently, so a first-run user is not asked about a folder they have never had

items.summary: Files has exactly three top-level directories: Cloud, 9to1 Local Workspace, This Machine.
items.verbatim_owner_request: so files should have 3 directories: - Cloud: Automatically connected when the user signs in - 9to1 Local Workspace: The 9to1 folder on the user's device - This Machine: The full folder system on a device. For devices for multiple ssds: ThisMachine-C:// ThisMachine-F:// etc. the user would click this machine and then see C:// F://

model.Cloud: present and automatically connected when the user signs in; absent or signed-out state must never block local creation or saving (the pinned correction that Boards creates and saves without an account)
model.9to1LocalWorkspace: the auto-created 9to1 folder under Documents from BF-39, one root per device, with per-app subfolders, and the relocation rule: if the user moves it, the app finds it by its stable root marker and re-registers there
model.ThisMachine: the device's real file system. Selecting it lists the devices' storage, then the folder tree under each. Multiple SSDs appear as separate entries (ThisMachine-C://, ThisMachine-F:// on Windows).

open_sub_decisions: Linux naming: this development PC and the ARM laptop have no C:// drives. Worker's chosen default, overridable by the owner: This Machine lists mounted volumes using the same shape, labelled by volume name and mount point (for example 'ThisMachine-nvme1n1p2 (/)' and 'ThisMachine-sda1 (/mnt/data)'), with drive letters used on Windows. Naming shown to the user for non-Windows mounts is the open point.
whether Cloud storage is a Files store in the same store/folder/file identity model Boards already writes through, or a mounted remote view behind that same boundary
whether per-app subfolders live inside 9to1 Local Workspace only, or also under a chosen alternate root

items.status: answered by owner 30 October 2026 — embed unmodified engines, fork modified ones
items.title: Browse must be built ON vendored engine donor sources, not against external binaries
items.verbatim_owner_request: Owner, 30 October 2026: 'I specifically told her to fork chromium and gecko and put the source directly inside of 9to1, and she said she did... The whole idea is that we take donor sources, put their source code into 9to1's repository, and then build upon those sources to save loads of time rebuilding from scratch.'
items.requirement: The durable principle already exists in AGENTS.md - donor engines may keep their implementation languages behind reviewed typed infrastructure boundaries, and donor licences and notices are preserved. What is missing is the requirement that the vendored source is actually FORKED and BUILT UPON. Today it is decoration.
measured_current_state: Gecko: '9to1 Workspace/Browse/Source/FirefoxGecko/' is a pinned SUBMODULE of a verbatim upstream mirror (CroakyJake12/gecko-dev) at upstream pin 5836a062726f715fda621338a17b51aff30d0a8c (.gitmodules; commit f775ea45 'Restore pinned Firefox donor source as the declared Browse submodule'). It is 4.1 GiB and includes devtools/ and layout/. No mozconfig, no moz.build entry, no project and NO production C# file in Browse references it ('9to1 Workspace/Browse/**' grep for FirefoxGecko|GeckoView|moz outside Source returns zero).

The repo documents this itself: '9to1 Workspace/Browse/README.md:70-74' - 'Firefox/Gecko remains the default, but no usable Gecko runtime supplier exists in this checkout... This source retrieval supplies no engine runtime.' 'docs/architecture/browse.md:106' - 'There is no maintained Gecko factory, real Gecko page-render evidence or Gecko...'.

Chromium: there is NO Chromium source anywhere in the repository. The only Chromium-specific path is .github/scripts/native16-arm64/chromium-native, which ACQUIRES prebuilt Debian binary packages (acquire-chromium-debian.py, chromium-pinned-manifest.json with schema keys selected_version/packages/archive_snapshots, chromium-soname-resolution.json). On Linux x64 the app instead launches an approved EXTERNAL system binary (ChromiumLocator.cs: /usr/bin/chromium, /usr/bin/chromium-browser, refusing anything unapproved), and this PC has neither installed, so Browse has no engine to attach to here (measured 30 October).
items.false_claim_on_record: A parallel worker reported having forked Chromium and Gecko into the repository. That claim is contradicted by the measurements above and, for Gecko, by the repo's own README. Retained as evidence of a verification failure, not as work. Reviewer countermeasure applied: parallel-lane claims stay labelled self-reported until a different session re-runs them.
items.conflicting_evidence: AGENTS.md permits mature donor engines behind reviewed boundaries, so vendoring is legitimate; but vendoring without building leaves a 4.1 GiB inert mirror plus an external-binary dependency, which is neither the owner's model nor a testable engine.
open_questions: Which engine is forked and built FIRST: Gecko (default per spec and vendored, but a full Firefox toolchain plus multi-tens-of-GB build environment is required, far beyond this machine's current ~8 GiB free against an 8 GiB reserve) or Chromium (not vendored at all today)?
Where does the engine build physically run - the PC, a separate build host, or a container/CI - and what is the retained toolchain and provenance contract for the built engine?

Do we keep an emergency path that attaches an approved system browser while no built fork exists, and if so how is that surface labelled to users and to evidence, so a measurement taken against a system browser is never reported as engine performance?

Which fork-level patches are in scope first - the ones that make unified DevTools real (the Linux engine currently throws NotSupportedException for in-process DevTools while the frontend lives in the vendored Gecko tree at Source/FirefoxGecko/devtools/), or engine capabilities the specification requires first?
items.affected_change: Everything in the Browse engine lane, the unified DevTools feature requested by the owner (F12 to the same DevTools on any screen, web or CUI), and the ARM64 package content. No engine-dependent claim should be reported as browser behaviour until a built fork exists.

items.title: Which donor copyleft exposures are acceptable, and is 9to1 distributed closed or open?
items.owner_intent: Take existing app work and build on top of it, re-doing the UI in CUI, keeping every non-proprietary feature or replacing it with a 9to1 equivalent (owner, 30 October 2026).
measured_facts: DuckDB (Data) MIT and Gecko (Browse) MPL-2.0/GPL-2.0/LGPL-2.1 tri-licence are usable; MPL election is the standard Firefox-derivative route and keeps our own code proprietary.
AppFlowy Board (Boards) is dual-licensed AGPL-3.0 OR MPL-2.0, so MPL election avoids AGPL.
Rnote (Canvas bridge, Canvas/rnote-poc) is GPL-3.0-or-later and is LINKED by our bridge, which puts GPL-3.0 copyleft on the combined Canvas engine boundary today.
Unsloth Studio is AGPL-3.0-only (5,659 SPDX headers) and its model browser is studio/backend/hub; only the unsloth core outside studio/ is Apache-2.0.
The installed Unsloth package has no frontend/Rust source and no Cargo/Tauri config, so it cannot be rebuilt natively as installed (our own migration notes say this).

Unsloth's own README and pyproject declare a DUAL model: the core unsloth package is Apache-2.0, optional components such as the Studio app are AGPL-3.0. Measured 5,659 AGPL-3.0-only SPDX headers in studio/ against 1 Apache-2.0, and 88 AGPL headers in studio/backend/hub (the model browser) with none others, so the browser is an AGPL extraction, not an Apache one.

Independent of licence, their browser cannot serve this PC's live model: models/tabs/hugging_face_tab.py states 'no support for PLE GGUFs', while the resident Strata host is launched with --ple-gguf on an IQ3_S shard. Their backend also ships its own llama.cpp model host, service router and tunnel/auth subsystems, which must not duplicate or displace the resident host.
